title: How AI Agents Access Demodesk Help Content for Smarter Support
summary: Demodesk's help content is accessible to AI agents via MCP and public URLs. See how Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot pull answers for faster customer support.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


Demodesk's help content is accessible to AI agents through three channels: a public MCP server at` mcp.demodesk.ai` , structured help articles at` demodesk.ai/help` , and an` llms.txt` index of canonical URLs. Any AI agent — Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or a custom agent built with AI Crew — can query, cite, and act on Demodesk documentation without a human in the loop. Two-thirds of customer service organizations now resolve routine questions through AI agents,[according to Salesforce's State of Service: AI Agents Edition](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/ai-customer-service-adoption-statistics) . The help content you expose to agents is now part of your support stack.


## Why AI agent access to help content matters now


AI agents handle a large and growing share of customer service work.[For teams running an AI agent in production, AI now closes around 40% of conversations without human involvement](https://crisp.chat/en/reports/state-of-ai-support/) , up from 22% in January 2026.[Mature autonomous agents resolve 50 to 80% of routine tickets end to end](https://www.richpanel.com/learn/ai-customer-service-statistics-2026) .


Those numbers only hold if the agent can find and understand your documentation. A help center locked behind a JavaScript-rendered chat widget, served from a subdomain the agent can't crawl, or structured for a human skimmer instead of a machine reader is invisible to the AI layer. That shows up as a support problem: slower first-touch resolution, more tickets escalated to humans, and customers who ask Claude or ChatGPT a question about your product and get a hallucinated answer instead of a cited one.


Demodesk made a deliberate architectural choice: our help content is machine-readable by default. Any AI agent — ours, a customer's, or a third-party assistant — can access it, cite it, and act on it.


## Three channels agents use to access Demodesk help content


### 1. MCP server (for agent-native access)


The Model Context Protocol server at[mcp.demodesk.ai](https://mcp.demodesk.ai/) is the primary access layer for autonomous agents. MCP is the open standard Claude, Cursor, and a growing set of agent frameworks use to query external tools and data sources.


Point an MCP-compatible agent at Demodesk's server and it can:


- Query help articles by topic, keyword, or product area
- Pull conversation data, call summaries, and CRM context when the user authorizes it
- Act on the record: update a field, draft a follow-up, trigger a workflow


Connecting is free on every Demodesk plan. You pay only for the AI compute you use. The agent you connect can be Claude, Microsoft Copilot, a custom agent built in AI Crew, or your own in-house stack.


### 2. Public help articles (for crawl-based access)


The Demodesk help center lives at[demodesk.ai/help](https://demodesk.ai/help) (English) and[demodesk.ai/de/hilfe](https://demodesk.ai/de/hilfe) (German). Articles are served as flat HTML pages with clean URLs —` /help/{slug}` — not inside a chat widget or JavaScript-only shell.


ChatGPT's browsing mode, Perplexity's crawler, Google's AI Overviews, and any agent making an HTTP request can read the content directly. No authentication required for public articles. No bot-detection wall.


The content was moved off Intercom into the main` .ai` site so AI agents could reach it. Previously, articles lived at` help.demodesk.com` behind Intercom's rendering layer, which worked for human readers but was opaque to most crawlers.


### 3.` llms.txt` index (for canonical URL discovery)


[demodesk.ai/llms.txt](https://demodesk.ai/llms.txt) is a curated index of canonical URLs for AI models. It tells an agent, in a few hundred lines of structured text: here are the pages that matter, here is what each one covers, here is the API documentation, here is the MCP endpoint.


This is the AI-era equivalent of a sitemap, written for LLMs instead of search crawlers. When an agent needs to answer “what does Demodesk's AI Coach do?” or “how do I connect HubSpot?”, it reads` llms.txt` first, picks the right canonical page, and cites it — instead of guessing or inventing a URL.


## How Demodesk uses this architecture internally


The same access layer powers Demodesk's own AI agents. When a Demodesk customer asks the AI Assistant a product question in-app, or an AI Crew agent needs context about a feature to complete a task, the agent queries the same MCP server and reads the same help content any external agent would read.


One source of truth. No divergence between internal and external documentation.


It also means improvements compound. When a help article gets rewritten for clarity, every AI agent — ours, Claude, ChatGPT, a customer's Copilot assistant — gets the better answer automatically. No separate AI training step. No model retraining. The content is the training.


## What this means for your support operation


If you're a RevOps or support leader evaluating how AI agents fit into your stack, the Demodesk approach illustrates three principles worth copying.


**Make the help content crawlable.**[43.6% of customer service teams now use AI across their service workflows, up from 32% in 2025](https://www.freshworks.com/customer-service/statistics/) . If your documentation is trapped in a chat widget or an authenticated knowledge base, the AI layer can't help your customers. Flat HTML, clean URLs, and a sitemap are the minimum.


**Publish an MCP endpoint.** The agent frameworks your customers already use — Claude Desktop, Cursor, Microsoft Copilot Studio — speak MCP. Exposing a server means an enterprise customer's RevOps team can wire your product into their internal agents without a custom integration project.


**Treat documentation as infrastructure.**[87% of customers say companies using GenAI for service must offer an option to reach a human agent, per Gartner's 2026 survey of 3,566 customers](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/customer-service-ai-statistics) . That's not a reason to avoid AI. It's a reason to make the AI layer accurate enough that escalation is the exception. Accuracy comes from the content, not the model.


## How Demodesk's AI agents act on this content


Access is the foundation. Action is the point.


The four pre-built Demodesk agents all use the same architecture:


- **AI Assistant** records every conversation — video, phone, in-person, field — and drafts the follow-up email with product details pulled from help content when relevant.
- **AI Coach** scores each call against your methodology — MEDDIC, BANT, or a custom scorecard — in seconds.
- **AI CRM Concierge** writes to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive with 99% field accuracy, approval before push.
- **AI Analyst** answers any question across your sales data: pipeline, deal risk, team performance.


Beyond the four, AI Crew lets you build unlimited custom autonomous agents that query the same MCP endpoint and act on the same record. Connect it to Claude, point it at Snowflake, trigger it on a schedule. No per-agent-run fee —[fair usage-based pricing, like the Claude or Perplexity API](https://demodesk.ai/pricing) .


One principle runs through the whole stack: the record of every conversation, portable to any AI, acted on automatically.
